change.title: pr-8
change.description: FIX: proper handling of group memberships
change.author: Régis Hanol

findings.title: Public members list silently truncated to 50 with no pager
findings.body: `members` now defaults `limit` to 50 (line 22) and the public template has no pagination controls (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs`). The previous code returned every member of a non-automatic group. A group with more than 50 members now shows only the first 50 with no indication. Either paginate the public page or keep the previous unlimited behaviour for non-automatic groups.
findings.originReason: The base applied limit/offset only when group.automatic?; this diff applies a default limit of 50 to all groups.

verification.reason: The default limit is now 50 for every group, and findMembers always sends limit 50. The public members template has no pager, so groups with more than 50 members get cut off with no sign of it. In the base, non-automatic groups returned every member.

findings.title: totalPages is off by one at exact multiples of the page size
findings.body: `totalPages` is `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. With 50 members and limit 50 it returns 2, so the pager shows '1/2' and Next requests offset 50, which returns an empty page. The same happens at 100, 150, and so on. `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)` gives the right count for every value and keeps the 0 case for empty groups.
findings.originReason: totalPages is new in this diff.

verification.reason: With user_count 50 and limit 50, Math.floor(50/50)+1 returns 2, so the pager shows a second page that is empty. Math.ceil would give the right count.

findings.title: Member removal bypasses the user_count counter cache
findings.body: `group.users.delete(user_id)` on a has_many :through association deletes join rows with a SQL delete, not callbacks. `GroupUser` declares `belongs_to :group, counter_cache: "user_count"` (`app/models/group_user.rb:2`), so the counter is not decremented and the stored `user_count` stays too high after a removal. The model already has `Group#remove`, which destroys each `group_users` record and runs the callback (`app/models/group.rb:276-278`). The admin list reads the stored value (`app/serializers/basic_group_serializer.rb:2`). The client refresh only corrects the value shown after a removal, not the stored column. Confidence is medium because it depends on how the installed Rails version handles has_many :through delete; I did not read the Gemfile.lock. Use `group.remove(user)` after loading the user, or check the counter after a removal.
findings.originReason: The base removed members through group.remove (destroy) or destroy_deletions (gu.destroy), and both run the counter cache callback; the new remove_member uses users.delete.

verification.reason: In Rails 4.1.8, `delete` on a has_many :through with no :dependent option removes the join rows with delete_all, so the belongs_to counter_cache callback on GroupUser never runs. The owner-side counter update looks for `users_count`/`group_users_count`, not `user_count`, so groups.user_count is never decremented. The base removed members by destroying GroupUser records (Group#remove / destroy_deletions).

findings.title: Adding an existing member can fail the whole request with no message
findings.body: `add_members` calls `group.add(user)` (`group.users.push`) for every name without checking membership. `group_users` has a unique index on (group_id, user_id) (`db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9`). Re-adding a current member, or sending a list that includes one, should raise a unique violation, which aborts the request. Names processed earlier in the loop stay saved because nothing is wrapped in a transaction. The client's `addMembers` has no failure handler (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/controllers/admin-group.js.es6:61-65`, `app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60`), so the admin sees nothing happen. The previous `Group#usernames=` diff (`app/models/group.rb:244-266`) avoided this. Filter out existing members before `add`. Confidence is medium because it depends on how the installed Rails version handles `push` on a has_many :through association for an existing row.
findings.originReason: The base UI saved membership through usernames=, which computed a diff. The new add_members endpoint that the UI now uses pushes every name without a check.

verification.reason: group.add calls users.push, which in Rails 4.1 builds and saves a new GroupUser with no membership check. GroupUser has no uniqueness validation, but there is a unique index on (group_id, user_id), so re-adding a member raises RecordNotUnique and the request returns a 500. The user-selector is not told to exclude current members, and the client's addMembers has no failure handler.

findings.title: create drops the alias level chosen in the form
findings.body: `create` sets only `name` and `visible` (lines 22-25). The form shows the alias-level combo box for new groups too (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:41-44`), and the client sends `alias_level` in `asJSON` (`app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:62-68`). The value is silently dropped and the group is saved with the default. `update` handles `alias_level` (line 37), so the same line belongs here. This predates the PR but this PR rewrote `create` and left the gap.
findings.originReason: The base create also set only name, usernames and visible, never alias_level.

verification.reason: create sets only name and visible, while the form shows the alias-level combo for new groups and asJSON sends alias_level, so the chosen value is dropped. The base create also ignored alias_level.

findings.title: Offset clamp leaves an empty page after the last member of a page is removed
findings.body: `findMembers` clamps the offset to `user_count`, which is the total before the reload. Removing the only member on page 2 of a 51-member group requests offset 50. The reload returns no rows, but the pager shows '2/2' over an empty list until the admin clicks Previous. The state is visible, not silent, and Previous recovers it. Clamping to the last valid page (`user_count - 1`, rounded to a page boundary) would avoid this. The offset also survives leaving and returning, because the admin group object is the shared record from the groups list (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/routes/admin_group_route.js:4-8`), so re-entering opens the last page viewed.
findings.originReason: Pagination and the offset clamp are new in this diff.

verification.reason: With 51 members, page 2 has offset 50. After the removal, findMembers clamps to min(51, 50) = 50 and the server returns an empty page with total 50. currentPage and totalPages both come out as 2 (also because of the floor+1 formula), so the pager shows '2/2' over an empty list. The group object comes from the shared groups list, so its offset carries over.

findings.title: remove_member guard test sends PUT to a DELETE route
findings.body: The automatic-group test for `remove_member` uses `xhr :put`, but the route is `delete "members"` (`config/routes.rb:49`). Controller specs call the action regardless of verb, so the test passes without checking the route it names. Use `:delete`. Nothing in the spec covers adding an existing member, the case in the add-members finding, or the alias level on create.
findings.originReason: The spec is new in this diff.

verification.reason: The route maps DELETE members to remove_member, but the guard spec uses xhr :put. Controller specs call the action directly whatever the verb, so the test never checks the route it names.

findings.title: Stale #group-users selector
findings.body: `input#group-users` (width 600px) no longer matches anything: the template now renders the user selector with `id="user-selector"` (`app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:28`). Update the selector or remove the rule.
findings.originReason: The template change in this diff dropped id="group-users", which left the rule stale.

verification.reason: The only element with id group-users was the user-selector in the base template. The head template renders it with id="user-selector", so the `input#group-users` rule no longer matches anything.

findings.title: Typed usernames are kept after Add and across groups
findings.body: `usernames` is never cleared after a successful add (the TODO on line 62 notes this), and the admin controller is a singleton, so the value is still bound to the selector when another group is opened. The admin would then add the previous group's names to the new group. The input shows those names, so this is visible rather than silent, but it is easy to click through. Reset `usernames` on success and when the route is set up.
findings.originReason: In the base, usernames was a computed property derived from the current members; the plain `usernames: null` property is new.

verification.reason: addMembers never resets `usernames` (see the TODO), and the route's setupController sets only the model on the singleton controller. Names typed for one group stay bound to the selector when another group is opened.

findings.title: Negative or non-numeric limit and offset produce database errors
findings.body: `limit` and `offset` are passed straight from `params` after `to_i` with no bounds. A negative value reaches SQL as LIMIT or OFFSET and the request fails with a 500. The endpoint is public. Clamp both values to sane ranges, for example limit 1..200 and offset at least 0.
findings.originReason: The base accepted unbounded limit/offset only for automatic groups; this diff extends it to every group.

verification.reason: Negative limit or offset values reach PostgreSQL as LIMIT/OFFSET, which rejects them, so the public endpoint returns a 500. The 'non-numeric' part is wrong, though: to_i turns those into 0, which gives no error.

contracts.action: Admin adds members: the Add button calls addMembers, which PUTs usernames to add_members and then reloads the list
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/group.rb:244-266 (Group#usernames=, the diff-based path the old save used)
contracts.before_after: Before: save sent a full usernames string and Group#usernames= diffed it, building or destroying group_users rows. After: each name is added with group.add (users.push) with no membership check.
contracts.visible_effect: On success the list reloads through findMembers, so the new members appear.
contracts.failure_mode: A name that is already a member can raise on the unique index (db/migrate/20130416004933_group_users.rb:9), giving a 500 with earlier names already saved. The client has no failure handler, so nothing is shown (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:51-60).
contracts.open_question: Does has_many :through push on an existing (group_id, user_id) row raise in the installed Rails version, or does it return silently? Read Gemfile.lock and the activerecord source for that version.

contracts.action: Admin removes a member: the X link asks for confirmation, then DELETEs user_id, then reloads
contracts.equivalent_path: app/models/group.rb:276-278 (Group#remove, which destroys each group_users record so callbacks run) and app/models/group.rb:258-263 (the old usernames= path, which destroyed group_users records)
contracts.before_after: Before: removal destroyed group_users records, which runs the GroupUser counter-cache callback. After: group.users.delete(user_id) on a has_many :through association.
contracts.visible_effect: The member is removed from the list and the reload corrects the count shown in the members heading.
contracts.failure_mode: If has_many :through delete skips callbacks, the stored user_count column (app/models/group_user.rb:2, the counter cache) is not decremented and the admin groups list shows a stale number. The client has no failure handler (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js:40-49). The remove link is also shown on automatic groups (see the group_member.hbs finding).
contracts.open_question: Does the installed Rails version's has_many :through delete run GroupUser callbacks (counter cache) or a delete_all? Confirm from the Gemfile.lock version and its activerecord source.

contracts.action: Admin pages the member list with Next and Previous, using offset and limit on the group object
contracts.equivalent_path: none (new behaviour; the old route loaded every member in afterModel)
contracts.before_after: Before: all members were fetched in afterModel and shown in full. After: one page of 50 is fetched per request, and the controller computes currentPage and totalPages.
contracts.visible_effect: The pager shows page and total, and the members heading shows the total count.
contracts.failure_mode: totalPages is one too high at exact multiples of the page size, so Next reaches an empty page. Removing the last member on the last page leaves an empty page (see the group.js finding).

contracts.action: Public group members tab opens (group.members route)
contracts.equivalent_path: the same route before this PR, which set controller model to the array from _members and rendered each m in model (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/templates/group/members.hbs before this PR)
contracts.before_after: Before: the route set controller model to an array and the template iterated model. After: the route sets model to the group and calls findMembers, and the template iterates members on the controller.
contracts.visible_effect: Expected: a table of members. Actual per the code read: header only, because the controller has no members property.
contracts.failure_mode: Empty list with no error. The rest of the group page still works.
contracts.open_question: Does Ember generate a plain Ember.Controller for the group.members route here, with no members property? If the generated controller proxies model, this is not a bug.

contracts.action: Public members page fetches the member list from /groups/:name/members.json
contracts.equivalent_path: the previous GroupsController#members (returned every member for non-automatic groups and capped automatic groups at 200 by default)
contracts.before_after: Before: non-automatic groups returned all members; automatic groups defaulted to 200. After: all groups default to 50 and return a {members, meta} object.
contracts.visible_effect: Only the first 50 members appear, with no pager on the public page.
contracts.failure_mode: Silent truncation of membership for groups above 50 members.

contracts.equivalent_path: the previous afterModel, which awaited findMembers before setup
contracts.before_after: Before: the route waited for members before rendering. After: it renders immediately and calls findMembers without waiting.
contracts.visible_effect: The members heading and list fill in after the request returns.
contracts.failure_mode: offset, limit, user_count and members live on the shared group object from the groups list (admin_group_route.js:4-8). Returning to a group opens the last page viewed and shows the previous members until the request completes. The failure of findMembers is not handled, so the list stays empty with no message.

contracts.action: Admin creates a new group (save on a group with no id)
contracts.equivalent_path: the previous create, which also did not set alias_level
contracts.before_after: Before and after: name and visible only. The client sends alias_level in the same payload.
contracts.visible_effect: The new group is created and the list is updated. The alias level chosen in the form is not kept.
contracts.failure_mode: alias_level silently falls back to the default (0).

contracts.action: Admin saves an existing group (save with an id, now PUT with top-level params)
contracts.equivalent_path: app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb:34-47 (the old update_put read nested group params and also handled usernames)
contracts.before_after: Before: nested group params with usernames in the same request. After: top-level name, alias_level and visible; membership goes through its own endpoints.
contracts.visible_effect: Name, visibility and alias level save. Automatic groups keep their name.
contracts.failure_mode: None found in the code read.

contracts.action: Remove link is rendered for each member in the admin list
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/admin/templates/group.hbs:25 (the Add members block, which uses {{#unless automatic}} in the controller context)
contracts.before_after: Before: the remove link was not rendered (members were managed in a single selector). After: the link is rendered per item.
contracts.visible_effect: An X next to each member. On automatic groups it should be hidden.
contracts.failure_mode: If bare automatic resolves against the User item, the link shows on automatic groups, and the server's 422 is not reported.
contracts.open_question: In Ember 1.x inside {{each}} with itemView, does a bare path such as automatic resolve against the item (member) or the controller?

contracts.action: Admin types usernames into the add-members selector and clicks Add
contracts.equivalent_path: app/assets/javascripts/discourse/components/user-selector.js.es6:52 (usernames is set only from autocomplete onChangeItems)
contracts.before_after: Before: usernames was a computed property built from the members list. After: usernames is set only when the user picks an autocomplete item.
contracts.visible_effect: Picked names are shown and can be added.
contracts.failure_mode: Names typed but not picked leave usernames empty, and addMembers returns with no message (admin-group.js.es6:63). The placeholder now says 'enter username', which suggests typing is enough.
contracts.open_question: Does the autocomplete plugin set the selected items for free-typed text when allowAny is not set? If not, the placeholder and the behaviour disagree.

contracts.action: Route get users removed from admin groups
contracts.equivalent_path: none; the removed route had no matching action in app/controllers/admin/groups_controller.rb
contracts.before_after: Before: GET /admin/groups/:id/users routed to a missing action. After: removed.
contracts.failure_mode: None: no JavaScript or Ruby caller of that path was found.

summary: Reviewed the 16 files in part 1 of PR pr-8 (admin and public group membership UI, the Admin::GroupsController and GroupsController actions, routes, the spec, locales and SCSS). The most serious issue is a likely blocker: the public group members tab now iterates `members` on a controller that does not define it, so the list renders empty. The rest are: a totalPages off-by-one (the pager goes to an empty page at exact multiples of 50); the remove link showing on automatic groups; a stored user_count that may go stale after removal because the removal bypasses the counter-cache callbacks; add-member failures that are not reported; the alias level being dropped on create; the public list silently truncated to 50 with no pager; and a few lower-severity items (a stale CSS selector, a test using the wrong verb, unvalidated limit/offset, and state that persists in the admin add-members input). Several contracts stay open because they depend on Ember or Rails behaviour that I did not read from vendored sources or the Gemfile.lock. Nothing was built or run.

entries.title: Public group members tab renders an empty list
entries.reason: The route has a model (the group), so Ember generates an ObjectController for it (ember.js generateControllerFactory picks 'object' when context is non-array). The route sets the group as the model, and findMembers sets `members` on the group, so `members` in the template is proxied to group.members and the rows render.
